learningObjective: Trace one full token sequence through per-head Q, K, and V projections, parallel attention, concatenation, and the output projection while tracking feature dimensions.
mediumRationale: A deterministic tensor SVG keeps the continuous sequence axis and split feature dimensions aligned through projection and recombination. Mermaid could show topology but not tensor widths and repeated per-head Q/K/V groupings precisely; semantic HTML would make dimensions accessible but weaken the split-and-concatenate geometry; interaction adds no necessary state; direct paper-figure reuse is unnecessary and reuse permission was not verified; mixed media adds complexity; and no visual leaves the crucial distinction between splitting features and splitting tokens implicit.

pages.insight: The decoder discussion distinguishes self-attention from cross-attention by identifying where queries, keys, and values originate.
The BERT material reinforces that transformer attention processes contextualized token sequences rather than assigning disjoint token subsets to heads.
The deck explicitly motivates multiple heads as different transformations or aspects of the same hidden features and notes scaled dot-product attention.

deckReview.notes: Slides 101 through 103 were reviewed independently. They motivate Q/K/V provenance and parallel views but do not trace the feature-dimension split through concatenation and output projection. The new visual isolates that missing tensor-shape lesson.

agentReview.summary: Recommended a phone-width vertical SVG with one shared sequence, two explicit representative heads plus an ellipsis for h heads, repeated Q/K/V labels in every shown head, and dimension labels at every split and merge.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG includes a title and complete description. Numbered stages, direct Q/K/V labels, repeated 'all n tokens' labels, tensor dimensions, solid arrows, distinct head outlines, and a text caption preserve the trace without color.
